title: Older Americans Month Community BINGO
source_title: 4 Days and Counting! | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: Every May, Older Americans Month recognizes the contributions of older adults, highlights aging trends, and reaffirms commitments to serve our older community members. The 2026 theme is “Champion Your Health”.Throughout the month of May, Oxford Seniors, Age-Friendly Oxford, and the Coalition for a Healthy Community, Oxford Area are partnering to highlight and offer programming focused on promoting physical, mental, and emotional health and well-being at all ages.You can participate by playing “Community BINGO” with us! It’s as easy as 1, 2, 3!1) Print your own or pick up a Community Bingo card at any of the following locations:Oxford Seniors, 922 Tollgate Dr., OxfordOxford Lane Library, 441 S. Locust St.The Knolls of Oxford, Clubhouse or Front DeskScripps Gerontology Center, 396 Upham Hall, on campus2) Every time you do something listed on the card, mark it off. The goal is to get “BINGO” as many times as possible. A “BINGO” is marking off any 5 squares in a straight line – either vertically, horizontally, or diagonally.3) Bring your completed BINGO card to the Intergenerational BINGO Party on Sun. May 31 from 3:00 – 5:00 p.m. at Oxford Seniors for prizes, snacks, and FUN! A PDF version of the BINGO card is attached to this message if you'd like to print one at home.

summary: May is **Older Americans Month** with the theme "Champion Your Health." Pick up a BINGO card at Oxford Seniors (922 Tollgate Dr.), Oxford Lane Library (441 S. Locust St.), or The Knolls of Oxford, complete activities listed on the card, and bring your completed card to the **Intergenerational BINGO Party on Sunday, May 31 from 3:00-5:00 p.m. at Oxford Seniors** for prizes and snacks. Get BINGO by marking off any 5 squares in a straight line (vertically, horizontally, or diagonally).

title: World Teen Mental Health Day Celebration
source_title: Spring Forward | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
2026 World Teen Mental Health Celebration at TMS
Monday, March 2nd was World Teen Mental Health Day. Started in 2020, this day focused on encouraging teens to talk openly about mental health and supporting mental health education. The Brave Initiative Team and the Sources of Strength Team at TMS created a plan and celebration for the student body.Thanks to bi3, Interact for Health, and the Joe Burrow Foundation, TMS received funding to provide each student with a "mental health toolkit". Throughout the school day, students received different items to help them think about strategies to stay mentally well and deal with life's stressors. From journaling to being physically active, students had the opportunity to think about what works best for them.During lunch on Monday, students will also had the opportunity to think about individuals in their lives who serve as mentors. These may be individuals at home, in school, or in the community. As a school, we created a display of all of the identified mentors.We encourage you to ask your student about this celebration. If you have any questions or want any additional information, please feel free to contact Talawanda Health & Wellness at 513.273.3390.Please enjoy this VIDEO of some of the events from the day.

summary: **Talawanda Middle School** celebrated **World Teen Mental Health Day on Monday, March 2nd** with activities organized by the Brave Initiative Team and Sources of Strength Team. Thanks to funding from **bi3, Interact for Health, and the Joe Burrow Foundation**, each student received a mental health toolkit with items promoting strategies like journaling and physical activity. Students also created a display honoring mentors in their lives during lunch. For more information, contact Talawanda Health & Wellness at **513.273.3390** or view the [VIDEO](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ) of the day's events.
